about: Phase 4 demo golden dataset (30 questions) over the 29-document EU digital-regulation corpus (corpus/manifest.json). Expands the mini-golden seed (mg-01..06, carried over verbatim) with 24 new entries across keyword, semantic, cross-document, hard, unanswerable, and multi-turn categories. Validated by atlas_evals.models.GoldenDataset.
verification: Expected documents and page ranges were derived from the ACTUAL ingested corpus — never invented. Each new entry was grounded read-only against the running Postgres/pgvector store: the chunk table's full-text index (websearch_to_tsquery + ts_rank_cd, the same keyword-search leg the app uses) and article-heading lookups were used to locate the operative provision, and expected_pages come from those chunks' start_page/end_page. The CONFIDENCE tag in notes records how firm each page range is; medium-confidence ranges have been widened by one page on each side to avoid false misses on operative-clause boundaries.
cross_document_scoring: For cross-document entries, expected_pages are scored against the PRIMARY (first-listed) expected_document only; the remaining expected_documents are credited at the document level (their operative locations are described in the entry notes). This is a schema v1 limitation — expected_pages is a single flat list, not keyed per document — and should be revisited if per-document page scoring is needed.

questions.question: What are the tasks of the data protection officer?
questions.notes: Keyword-heavy: the distinctive phrase 'data protection officer' and 'tasks' appear verbatim in GDPR Art 37-39 (pp. 55-56), so websearch_to_tsquery matches and keyword search ranks GDPR at #1 — as do vector and hybrid. Guards against a chunking/RRF change silently regressing exact-term retrieval.

questions.question: If software or a streaming service I paid for does not work as advertised, what can I demand from the trader?
questions.notes: Semantic paraphrase: the colloquial wording ('doesn't work as advertised', 'demand from the trader') shares almost no rare terms with the legal text ('conformity', 'remedies', Art 14, remedies pp. 22-25; conformity basis ~p. 13), so keyword search misses entirely while vector returns the Digital Content Directive across the whole top-5. The clearest vector-beats-keyword case in the set.

questions.question: How quickly must an essential-services operator notify authorities after a serious security incident?
questions.notes: Incident-notification timelines appear across several cybersecurity instruments. NIS2 (Art 23, 24h early warning / 72h notification, pp. 49-51) is the primary/current source; nis1.pdf (the predecessor, ~pp. 20-22) is an acceptable secondary, and dora.pdf / cra.pdf carry ICT- and product-specific reporting. expected_document is the primary — Phase 4 should credit all acceptable sources.

questions.question: What must the crypto-asset white paper for an asset-referenced token contain?
questions.notes: Hard: precise MiCA jargon ('asset-referenced token', 'crypto-asset white paper') buried in a 166-page document, and the full-sentence phrasing defeats keyword search (all content words must co-occur in one chunk). Vector and hybrid rank MiCA #1; keyword returns nothing. Exercises retrieval precision on the largest document (further detail lives in annexes ~pp. 148-153).

questions.question: What is the recommended daily amount of water an adult should drink?
questions.notes: Out-of-corpus (health/nutrition, not EU digital regulation). The top vector score should be low (~0.2 observed) versus ~0.77 for answerable questions — the signal a Phase 4 abstention check would threshold on. Note: topically-adjacent unanswerables (e.g. US HIPAA/CCPA) score higher (~0.5) because the corpus's US adequacy decisions overlap, so this seed deliberately uses a clean off-domain case.

questions.question: What does the AI Act consider a high-risk AI system?
questions.notes: Known-hard query that exists to permanently track a fusion behaviour. The Article 6 high-risk classification chunks are indexes 38 (p. 14, classifying recital), 138 (pp. 53-54), and 139/141/142 (pp. 54-56). CORRECTION (verified via GET /api/chunks): index 138 is a DEFINITIONAL chunk — it contains Article 6(1)-(3), the classification test itself. It merely OPENS with the tail of Article 5 (annual reporting on real-time remote biometric identification), which is all its 300-char snippet shows; an earlier analysis mistook the snippet for the whole chunk and wrongly labelled 138 a term-dense distractor. Vector correctly ranks 138 #1. Keyword's AND-semantics never surface it, so it appears in the vector list only; hybrid RRF therefore demotes it out of the top 5. That is a mild fusion cost, not a win: hybrid's top 4 are still the other Article-6 chunks (38, 142, 139, 141). Expected chunk indexes for page-level matching: 138 joins 38/139/141/142.

questions.question: What is the right to erasure under the GDPR?
questions.notes: Why: exercises exact-term retrieval of a named GDPR right ('right to erasure' / 'right to be forgotten', Art 17). Verified: FTS-ranked gdpr.pdf for 'right to erasure without undue delay' -> top chunk index 95 (pp. 43-44), whose content is the Art 17 operative text. CONFIDENCE: high.

questions.question: What are the rules for affixing the CE marking to a product with digital elements?
questions.notes: Why: 'CE marking' is a distinctive term keyword search should nail. Verified: heading lookup in cra.pdf found chunk 114 (p. 48) containing 'Article 30 Rules ... for affixing the CE marking' preceded by the conformity-assessment obligation in chunk 113 (pp. 47-48). CONFIDENCE: high.

questions.question: What is a statement of reasons under the Digital Services Act?
questions.notes: Why: 'statement of reasons' is DSA-specific terminology (Art 17) sitting alongside notice-and-action (Art 16). Verified: heading/phrase lookup in dsa.pdf located the operative provisions in chunks 111-113 (pp. 50-52). CONFIDENCE: high.

questions.question: When is an undertaking designated as a gatekeeper under the Digital Markets Act?
questions.notes: Why: 'gatekeeper' + 'designated' is the DMA's signature term (Art 3). Verified: FTS-ranked dma.pdf for the designation thresholds -> operative cluster at chunks 66-68 (pp. 30-31, the quantitative-threshold presumptions). CONFIDENCE: medium — document certain; the designation criteria also restate in nearby recitals. Range widened ±1 (to pp. 29-32) to avoid false misses on the operative-clause boundary.

questions.question: What is the European Digital Identity Wallet?
questions.notes: Why: 'European Digital Identity Wallet' is the defining term of the eIDAS2 amendment. Verified: FTS-ranked eidas2.pdf -> densest wallet-provisioning cluster at chunks 81-83 (pp. 40-42). CONFIDENCE: medium — eIDAS2's inserted-article numbering (Art 5a etc.) is intricate; the term is also defined earlier (Art 3, ~p. 6), so retrieval to the p. 6 definition should also count. Range widened ±1 (to pp. 39-43) to avoid false misses on the operative-clause boundary.

questions.question: What are the assurance levels of a European cybersecurity certificate?
questions.notes: Why: 'assurance level' ('basic'/'substantial'/'high') is precise Cybersecurity Act terminology. Verified: FTS-ranked cybersecurity-act.pdf for 'European cybersecurity certificate assurance level' -> top chunk 83 (pp. 42-43) stating the three levels. CONFIDENCE: high.

questions.question: What must an online intermediation service do when it suspends or terminates a business user's account?
questions.notes: Why: the P2B Regulation's 'restriction, suspension and termination' rules (Art 4) with a statement of reasons. Verified: phrase lookup in p2b-regulation.pdf -> operative chunk 33 (pp. 14-15). CONFIDENCE: high.

questions.question: Can I get a copy of my data from one service in a reusable format and move it to a competitor?
questions.notes: Why: colloquial paraphrase of the right to data portability (GDPR Art 20) with no legal terms in the query. Verified: 'machine-readable format' (the exact Art 20(1) phrase) occurs only in chunk 98 (p. 45), with the lead-in on chunk 97 (pp. 44-45). CONFIDENCE: high.

questions.question: I'm unhappy with my cloud provider — can I move my data and applications to a competing service, and who pays?
questions.notes: Why: everyday phrasing of the Data Act's 'switching between data processing services' chapter. Verified: FTS-ranked data-act.pdf -> strong operative cluster at chunks 56, 60, 61 (pp. 23-26, switching obligations and charges). CONFIDENCE: high (highest FTS ranks in the set).

questions.question: Does a website need my permission before storing cookies on my device?
questions.notes: Why: lay phrasing of the ePrivacy consent-for-terminal-equipment rule (Art 5(3)). Verified: 'terminal equipment' + cookie consent language clusters in chunk 13 (pp. 5-6) of the 11-page directive. CONFIDENCE: medium — the operative Art 5(3) and its recital 25 are close together on pp. 3-6. Range widened ±1 (to pp. 4-7) to avoid false misses on the operative-clause boundary.

questions.question: What does a company have to do to manage its cybersecurity risks under the new EU rules?
questions.notes: Why: paraphrase of NIS2's cybersecurity risk-management measures (Art 21) — distinct from the incident-notification timeline in mg-03. Verified: FTS-ranked nis2.pdf for 'cybersecurity risk-management measures essential entities' -> cluster at chunks 34-37 (pp. 16-18). CONFIDENCE: medium — this region includes both the measures and their framing recitals; the numbered Art 21 list may extend slightly beyond p. 18. Range widened ±1 (to pp. 15-19) to avoid false misses on the operative-clause boundary.

questions.question: Do online shops have to be usable by blind and partially sighted people?
questions.notes: Why: everyday phrasing of the European Accessibility Act's accessibility requirements for e-commerce services. Verified: Art 2 scope brings 'e-commerce services' into scope (chunk 32, pp. 14-15), and the operative accessibility requirements for e-commerce services — identification/e-signature/payment made perceivable, operable, understandable and robust — are in Annex I, chunks 71-72 (pp. 34-35). CONFIDENCE: high (operative Annex I requirement located; earlier flagged approximation resolved).

questions.question: Are video-sharing platforms required to protect children from harmful videos?
questions.notes: Why: paraphrase of the AVMSD amendment's duty on video-sharing platforms to protect minors (Art 28b). Verified: the operative Art 28b measures are at chunks 46-48 (pp. 20-22) — chunk 47 (p. 21) 'For the purposes of the protection of minors ...' and chunk 48 (pp. 21-22) the minors' personal-data safeguards; the earlier p. 2 mention (chunk 3) was the recital. CONFIDENCE: high (operative Art 28b located; earlier flagged approximation resolved).

questions.question: Can researchers automatically analyse large amounts of copyrighted text and data for a study?
questions.notes: Why: paraphrase of the DSM Copyright Directive's text-and-data-mining exception for research (Arts 3-4). Verified: the directive's articles sit after long recitals (pp. 1-21); the operative TDM exceptions are Art 3 (research organisations, lawful access, secure storage — chunk 51, pp. 22-23) and Art 4 (general TDM exception with machine-readable rights reservation — chunk 52, p. 23). CONFIDENCE: high (operative Arts 3-4 located; earlier pp. 3-5 were recitals).

questions.question: What rules govern sending personal data to companies outside the EU?
questions.notes: Why: international transfers span the GDPR's Chapter V (Arts 44-49) and the Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses decision (the SCC instrument itself). Verified: FTS-ranked gdpr.pdf for third-country transfer safeguards -> Chapter V cluster at chunks 128-133 (pp. 61-64); scc-decision.pdf is the whole SCC instrument (clauses near pp. 6-7, chunk 14). expected_pages are the GDPR primary region (see cross_document_scoring); scc-decision is credited at document level. CONFIDENCE: medium. Range widened ±1 (to pp. 60-65) to avoid false misses on the operative-clause boundary.

questions.question: How can a product or service get certified as cybersecure under EU law?
questions.notes: Why: EU cybersecurity certification is defined by the Cybersecurity Act's certification framework (primary) and referenced by the Cyber Resilience Act's conformity route for products. Verified: cybersecurity-act.pdf certificate/assurance-level provisions at chunk 83 (pp. 42-43, same operative text as dg-k06); cra.pdf conformity assessment (~pp. 47-48) is the secondary. expected_pages are the primary (see cross_document_scoring); cra credited at document level. CONFIDENCE: medium. Range widened ±1 (to pp. 41-44) to avoid false misses on the operative-clause boundary.

questions.question: What EU rules let me move my data and workloads between different service providers?
questions.notes: Why: portability/switching spans the Data Act's switching chapter (primary) and the Free Flow of Non-Personal Data Regulation's porting/self-regulatory codes. Verified: data-act.pdf switching cluster at chunks 56/60/61 (pp. 23-26, same as dg-s02); free-flow-non-personal-data.pdf (10-page regulation) is the secondary. expected_pages are the primary; free-flow credited at document level. CONFIDENCE: high (primary).

questions.question: What rules govern re-using data held by the public sector?
questions.notes: Why: re-use of public-sector information is governed by the Open Data Directive (primary) and, for protected categories, the Data Governance Act. Verified: FTS-ranked open-data-directive.pdf for 're-use of documents' -> chunks 19-21 (pp. 8-9); dga.pdf re-use-of-protected-data provisions are the secondary. expected_pages are the primary (see cross_document_scoring); dga credited at document level. CONFIDENCE: medium — open-data region includes recitals framing the general principle; document certain. Range widened ±1 (to pp. 7-10) to avoid false misses on the operative-clause boundary.

questions.question: How often must a financial entity carry out threat-led penetration testing under DORA?
questions.notes: Why: 'threat-led penetration testing' (TLPT, Arts 26-27) is precise jargon buried in a 79-page regulation; full-sentence phrasing defeats keyword AND-semantics. Verified: operative TLPT provisions at chunks 93-94 (pp. 45-46, 'penetration testing ... TLPT ... financial entity') — distinct from the earlier recital mention (p. 11). CONFIDENCE: high.

questions.question: What is the crisis response mechanism for very large online platforms?
questions.notes: Why: the DSA 'crisis response mechanism' (Art 36) is a narrow VLOP provision easily confused with risk-assessment/mitigation articles. Verified: operative provision at chunks 137-138 (pp. 65-67). CONFIDENCE: high.

questions.question: What does HIPAA require for protecting patient health records in the United States?
questions.notes: Why: the topically-ADJACENT unanswerable (like the water-intake note's HIPAA caveat) — US health-privacy law, not EU digital regulation. Verified: 'HIPAA' appears only incidentally (3 chunks, all in adequacy-us-dpf.pdf) and the corpus contains none of HIPAA's requirements, so it is genuinely unanswerable while retrieval may surface US-privacy-adjacent chunks at moderate scores. Exercises abstention against a near-miss.

questions.question: What are the requirements of the California Consumer Privacy Act for selling personal information?
questions.notes: Why: a second topically-ADJACENT unanswerable — US state privacy law. Verified: no chunk contains the California Consumer Privacy Act's provisions (only incidental US-privacy context in the adequacy decisions). Complements dg-u01 and mg-05 (clean off-domain) to cover the distant/adjacent spectrum for abstention.

questions.question: And who is actually required to appoint one?
questions.notes: Why: tests coreference across turns — 'one' resolves to the data protection officer from the setup turn; the follow-up targets the DPO DESIGNATION rule (Art 37), not the tasks (Art 39). Verified: 'shall designate a data protection officer' operative text in chunks 114-115 (pp. 54-55). CONFIDENCE: high. Depends on conversation history being replayed.

setup_turns.question: What are the tasks of the data protection officer?

questions.question: What obligations does its provider have?
questions.notes: Why: 'its provider' resolves to the provider of a high-risk AI system from the setup turn; targets the AI Act's obligations of providers of high-risk systems (Chapter III, Section 3). Verified: FTS-ranked ai-act.pdf for provider obligations -> cluster at chunks 154-156 (pp. 61-63). CONFIDENCE: medium — the provider-obligation articles span several pages. Range widened ±1 (to pp. 60-64) to avoid false misses on the operative-clause boundary. Depends on conversation history being replayed.
